Results are ranked using training data only. Holdout segments restart with fresh capital, flat positions and their own indicator warmup. Repeatedly choosing settings based on holdout results makes that data part of your selection process. “Load” runs the selected settings on the full chart; its results will differ from the split tests.

Know what your backtest measures

Signals use completed candles. Orders execute at the next candle’s open. One long position at a time; no leverage or short selling. Position size is a percentage of available cash, including the entry fee.

Fees and adverse slippage apply on both entry and exit. Stops and targets are measured from the entry fill. Gaps fill at the open. When both stop and target are touched in one candle, the stop takes priority. Remaining positions close at the final candle.

Equity is marked at candle close; drawdown does not measure intrabar losses. Buy & hold is a gross price comparison without costs. Chart aggregation changes the display only; tests always use the original imported candles.

Sample candles are synthetic and are not historical market prices. Fetch real candles using the market controls, or import your own time-ordered OHLCV CSV for meaningful research. Forex and commodity tests simulate unleveraged spot exposure, not broker lots or futures contracts. No currency conversion is performed; initial capital and P&L use the pair’s quote currency. This browser chart has no Pine Script support or broker connection. Open Trading operations for the separate Django-backed recording, paper trading and controlled execution system. Market data refreshes only when you fetch it. Binance candles are checked against exchange server time; Twelve Data’s newest candle is always omitted to avoid testing an unfinished session.

Start with a hypothesis.

  1. Choose a market, symbol and timeframe, then fetch candles. Forex and commodities require your Twelve Data key. CSV import and synthetic samples remain available.
  2. Choose an SMA crossover, RSI, or custom rule strategy.
  3. Set your capital, fees, slippage, and exit levels.
  4. Run the test and inspect every trade.

CSV header: time,open,high,low,close,volume. Use ISO dates or Unix timestamps, oldest first. Volume is optional. Dates with times should include a timezone.

Strategies and your latest imported dataset are saved in this browser. Installation requires HTTPS and a supporting browser. After the first online visit, the app works offline.

Custom rules compare price, SMA, or RSI using above, below, or cross conditions. This app does not run Pine Script.
